facts.text: A default graph reports format 1, root s-root, an 8-character seed, max_nodes 500 and depth 1.
Hop 1 subjects come in ordinal id order as s-root, s-core, s-other, s-sh1, s-sh2 and s-web, with the boundary subject s-far last.
At depth zero the graph lists only s-root as a subject and still reports at least one truncated edge.
At depth 2 both s-lib and f-lib-1 are admitted and the f-web-1 to f-lib-1 ref becomes a fact edge.
With facts false the graph holds no facts, keeps only contains edges and lists the subjects s-root, s-core and s-web.
The full seeded graph has 13 nodes and every maxNodes value from 1 upward yields exactly the smaller of max and total.
With maxNodes 4 the subjects are s-root, s-core, s-other and s-sh1, no facts are admitted and truncated subjects exceeds zero.
A depth-0 request on s-lib returns s-lib, s-core and s-root, and with maxNodes 2 it clamps to s-lib and s-core with truncated subjects 1.
The boundary subject s-far is last in the subject list, is the only subject carrying boundary, and its inbound edges come from f-core-1 and f-core-2.
With maxNodes 12 the subject s-far is hidden, the graph holds 12 nodes and truncated subjects is 1.
A mentions of the duplicated name Shared links both s-sh1 and s-sh2, and both edges carry ambiguous true.
The root resolves from the name Acme and, after case and whitespace are folded, from the alias Acme Docs to s-root.
With no subject the tree mode returns a null root, 100 subjects, no facts and truncated subjects 200.
The seed is unchanged when a new fact is posted and changes for depth 2, maxNodes 50 or facts false.
Depth 4 and -1 are rejected as bad_depth, maxNodes 0 and 2001 as bad_max_nodes, and the unknown subject nobody as subject_not_found.
Within FromQuery the facts value maybe is rejected as bad_facts and the max_nodes value lots as bad_max_nodes.
A slot ref to the occupied key owner resolves to fact f-core-2, while the empty key on Web falls back to subject s-web.
The external symbol ref stays on fact f-root-1 as unresolved and the unknown target f-ghost is reported with reason not_found.
In the bounded boundary query a cap of 20 nodes admits s-root and 18 referrers, and truncated subjects and edges are both 42.
The inbound_slot row probe reads at most one row because the slot query only reads keys an admitted fact occupies.
At maxNodes 12 the hidden f-far-1 refs are reported as confirms and mentions with reason not_admitted, and truncated edges is 3.
With maxNodes 2 on s-a only fa-1 is admitted, truncated facts and edges are each 1, and the hidden fa-2 to fa-1 ref is not_admitted.
A fact with 2100 dangling refs yields 2000 unresolved entries and truncated unresolved 100, with no truncated edges.
The facts parameter accepts true, True, TRUE and 1 as true and false, False, FALSE and 0 as false, rejecting yes, 2, tru and padded values as bad_facts.
A 500-character text is unchanged while 501 characters keeps 499 and adds an ellipsis, and a surrogate pair on the cut is dropped whole.
From s-b the parent chain admits s-a but does not expand it, so s-c stays unreachable even at depth 3.
In tree mode a cycle has no root, so no subject is drawn and truncated subjects is 3.
The committed fixture graph-api.json must equal the depth-2 API output byte for byte, and DOSSIER_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 rewrites it.
GraphSeed seeds one slot row that points the note key owner of s-core at fact f-core-2.
Populate takes a reverse flag and inserts the subjects and facts in the opposite order so insert order cannot change the output.
at: foreach (var subject in reverse ? Subjects.Reverse() : Subjects)

facts.text: PopulateTree makes the first 20 subjects roots and gives each later subject a parent indexed by (i - 20) divided by 3.
GraphSeed carries the hostile strings EvilImg, EvilJs and EvilScript through the fixture so the page harness proves they only ever reach the output as text.
at: public const string EvilImg = "";

facts.text: GraphSeed.Bulk is a throwaway writer that shares one connection and transaction and commits them in Dispose.
A search for alpha returns 2 hits and includes both the fact with alpha in its text and the fact carrying alpha only as a tag.
A text hit scores below a tag-only hit for the same term and ranks first, because text weight 10 beats tag weight 3.
A subject filter of MEMOS ui and one of memos each match the single fact by name casefold and by alias.
Direction in on a fact ref target returns only the pointer fact that references the target, not the target itself.
Direction out on the pointer fact returns the single fact that it references.
A ref target that is an external URL is rejected with the code ref_target_not_internal.
Posting two facts under the key state leaves the first out of default search results while the second is returned.
Status superseded returns only the older fact and status live returns only the newer one.
Paging five facts with limit 2 through the cursor yields five distinct ids and a final Complete true.
With limit 2 over five facts the response has 2 hits, a Total of 5 and Complete false.
A limit of 1 over three facts is incomplete, offers a Next cursor and a Refine text that mentions subject.
A search hit carrying a query score has a null Section and a null Cites.
After a Retract the retracted fact is absent from default search results while the kept fact is present.
Show on the pointer fact returns one ref to the target and one attachment whose Sha256 is the fixture sha.
Show of an unknown fact id returns null.
A brief hit exposes exactly id, kind, status and text, and the long text is cut to 121 characters ending in an ellipsis.
A brief search keeps the same Total, Complete and Next as the full search, and the second page returns 2 hits.
Direction in on a symbol target returns both facts citing that symbol, while direction out is rejected with ref_target_not_internal.
at: var caught = Assert.Throws<DossierRequestException>(() => db.Store.Search(new SearchRequest { RefTarget = Sym, Direction = "out" }));

facts.text: Posting facts in another subject that cite a symbol leaves the compiled fact ids and their scores unchanged.
Each plain-text argument pair expects exactly one hit whose text equals the expected string.
Real FTS5 syntax still works: alpha OR gamma yields 2 hits and alpha NOT beta yields 0.
A query with an unbalanced quote is reported as invalid_query.
The tag filter query tags:ui-kit returns exactly one expected hit, the fact tagged ui-kit.
